title: Determination of the Total Acid Number (TAN) in Crude Oils
author: Jonas Sundberg
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wvcfe2w

steps.title: Set up titrator in fume hood
steps.instruction: Place the TitroLine 7750 titrator inside a ventilated fume‑hood, connect the power cable and verify the system starts, attach an optional keyboard for sample entry, insert a USB memory stick (no encryption) for PDF result storage, and enable low‑speed stirring (stir bar must not touch the electrode) for all subsequent steps.

steps.title: Prepare KOH titrant solution
steps.instruction: Measure 6.0 g potassium hydroxide (KOH) and transfer to a 1 L glass flask, add 1000 mL 2‑propanol, stir overnight at room temperature, filter through a glass funnel if cloudy, label with contents and preparation date, and use within one month. The solution contains 6 g KOH L⁻¹ (≈0.1 M).

steps.title: Prepare titration solvent
steps.instruction: Measure 500 mL toluene in a 500 mL volumetric flask and transfer to a 1 L glass bottle. In a separate 500 mL volumetric flask add 5.0 mL de‑gassed Milli‑Q water, top up with 2‑propanol to 500 mL, and combine this mixture with the toluene bottle. Label the bottle with contents and preparation date. The solvent composition is 500:495:5 (toluene:2‑propanol:H₂O).

steps.title: Rinse titrant bottle and fluidics
steps.instruction: Rinse the titrant bottle sequentially with Milli‑Q water then 2‑propanol, fill with the KOH titrant (≈50 mL for initiation, 5–6 mL per analysis) and place on the bottle holder. Rinse the solvent syringe, tubing and automatic pipette with titrant solution, select the ‘Rinsing’ method on the software and perform three 10 mL rinses.

steps.title: Calibrate titrant with KHP
steps.instruction: Prepare three calibration solutions: weigh ~125 mg potassium hydrogen phthalate (KHP) into a 100 mL beaker, add 50 mL water and ultrasonicate until dissolved. For each solution, place the beaker on the titrator, select ‘Mode → Titer KOH → Start’, enter the exact KHP mass, discard the solution and rinse the electrode with water. Repeat for all three solutions; the instrument stores the average concentration (expected 0.09–0.11 M, ≈0.1 M). If the average deviates strongly, troubleshoot titrant, KHP or instrument.

steps.title: Optional KHPT calibration
steps.instruction: Fill a 25 mL beaker with 20 mL freshly prepared aqueous potassium hydrogen phthalate (0.2 g per 80 mL). Select ‘Mode → Titer KOH → Start’, enter the measured KHPT mass, discard the solution, and repeat the calibration three times. The calculated titrant concentration should be ≈0.1 M; large deviations indicate a problem.

steps.title: Blank instrument with solvent
steps.instruction: Add approximately 125 mL (or 100 mL as alternative) of the titration solvent to a 250 mL beaker with a stirrer, select ‘Mode → Blank TAN‑TBN → Start’, and repeat the blank once (or twice). After each blank, discard the solution and rinse the electrode with titration solvent, water, and titration solvent again.

steps.title: Verify performance with QC sample
steps.instruction: Weigh ~20 g (≈25 mL) of a QC crude‑oil sample into a 250 mL beaker, record the weight to two decimals, dissolve in 125 mL titration solvent (500:495:5), select ‘Mode → TAN ASTM 664 → Start’, enter the measured mass, and record the result. The measured TAN must be within ±10 % of 0.5 mg KOH g⁻¹; otherwise troubleshoot before proceeding.

steps.title: Determine TAN of crude oil samples
steps.instruction: For each oil sample, weigh ~20 g (≈25 mL) into a 250 mL beaker, record the exact mass, dissolve in 100 mL titration solvent, select ‘Mode → TAN ASTM 664 → Start’, enter the sample weight, date and sample name, and run the titration. After measurement, discard the solution and rinse the electrode sequentially with titration solvent, water, and titration solvent. Repeat for all samples.

steps.title: Prepare fatty‑acid mixture (optional)
steps.instruction: Weigh tridecanoic acid (53.6 mg, 0.25 mmol), pentadecanoic acid (60.6 mg, 0.25 mmol) and heptadecanoic acid (67.6 mg, 0.25 mmol) into a 100 mL glass flask. Measure 20.0 mL toluene, transfer to a 100 mL volumetric flask and top up with hexadecane to obtain an 80:20 hexadecane:toluene mixture (density ≈820 g L⁻¹, 100 mL ≈82 g). Add the solvent mixture to the flask containing the fatty acids and ultrasonicate for 10 min. The 0.75 mmol total fatty acid corresponds to 42.08 mg KOH (0.51 mg KOH g⁻¹).

steps.title: Store instrument after analysis
steps.instruction: Rinse the electrode with titration solvent and water; if any solid material is present, remove it with a lint‑free Kimwipe. Remove the titrant bottle and replace it with a bottle of fresh Milli‑Q water. Place an empty beaker under the pipette, select ‘Mode → Rinsing → Start’, and perform three consecutive 10 mL rinses, discarding waste. Finally, turn off the titrator and disconnect all power cables.
